## One-Sentence Summary

A mobile app that uses AI-powered video analysis to deliver sprint coaching feedback anytime, helping athletes improve form while enabling coaches and parents to track progress.

## Problem

The creators describe a consistent gap in sprint training: athletes often practice without timely feedback, while coaches lack bandwidth to analyze every block start or sprint repetition---especially when juggling other jobs or when athletes are traveling or on school breaks. This leaves athletes without guidance to progress safely and effectively when direct coaching isn't available.

## Solution / Product Overview

The product is presented as "a sprint coach in your pocket." It analyzes user-submitted sprint videos with AI to provide actionable feedback at any time. The aim is to let athletes see what's happening in their sprints, help coaches extend their impact without slowing practice, and assure parents that training is progressing safely.

## Key Features & Capabilities

-   AI-powered video analysis of sprints.

-   Feedback on block starts.

-   Analysis of shin and torso angles.

-   Insights into max-velocity mechanics.

-   Positioning as a tool to complement---not replace---human coaching.

## Target Users & Use Cases

The campaign calls out athletes who train alone or while traveling, coaches seeking scalable analysis during practice, and parents looking for confidence in safe, continuous improvement.

## Development Status

The team states it has a working demo. Funds are intended to "complete and polish" the app into a user-ready tool, with a launch planned for the first wave of athletes, coaches, and parents.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan

Planned milestones include: finalizing the app, building specified analysis features (block starts, angle analysis, max-velocity mechanics), partnering with athletes/coaches/influencers to spread the word, and launching to an initial user group. The estimated delivery is December 2025, with a contingency that delivery could shift slightly into January 2026. If timelines shift, the team commits to immediate notifications and monthly progress updates during development.

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds

Most funds are allocated to app development, with additional support for launch preparation and marketing. The team notes a buffer for unexpected costs to keep development the top priority.

## Risks & Challenges

The team cites typical software development risks such as potential delays or technical issues, mitigated by a scoped plan and monthly updates. Because rewards are mostly digital (codes or access), fulfillment risk is described as low, though minor delays in distributing access could occur. A health and wellness disclaimer clarifies that the project is not a substitute for medical treatment or diagnosis.

## Team & Partnerships

The effort is led by a sprint coach ("the founders"). The team plans to collaborate with athletes, coaches, and influencers to expand reach.

## What's Included

Backers receive primarily digital rewards, such as access codes.

## Technical Details

The campaign labels the technology as patent pending and repeatedly emphasizes AI-based video analysis for sprint mechanics. No device, OS, or hardware specs are provided.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans

The team promises ongoing updates during development and indicates that improvements will be delivered through the app over time.

## One-Sentence Summary

A mobile app that uses AI-powered video analysis to deliver sprint coaching feedback anytime, helping athletes improve form while enabling coaches and parents to track progress.

## Problem

The creators describe a consistent gap in sprint training: athletes often practice without timely feedback, while coaches lack bandwidth to analyze every block start or sprint repetition---especially when juggling other jobs or when athletes are traveling or on school breaks. This leaves athletes without guidance to progress safely and effectively when direct coaching isn't available.

## Solution / Product Overview
The product is presented as "a sprint coach in your pocket." It analyzes user-submitted sprint videos with AI to provide actionable feedback at any time. The aim is to let athletes see what's happening in their sprints, help coaches extend their impact without slowing practice, and assure parents that training is progressing safely.

## Key Features & Capabilities
- AI-powered video analysis of sprints.
- Feedback on block starts.
- Analysis of shin and torso angles.
- Insights into max-velocity mechanics.
- Positioning as a tool to complement---not replace---human coaching.

## Target Users & Use Cases
The campaign calls out athletes who train alone or while traveling, coaches seeking scalable analysis during practice, and parents looking for confidence in safe, continuous improvement.

## Development Status
The team states it has a working demo. Funds are intended to "complete and polish" the app into a user-ready tool, with a launch planned for the first wave of athletes, coaches, and parents.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan
Planned milestones include: finalizing the app, building specified analysis features (block starts, angle analysis, max-velocity mechanics), conducting a planned, limited pilot test with a specific, named high school or club track team to validate the app in a real-world coaching environment before full launch, partnering with athletes/coaches/influencers to spread the word, and launching to an initial user group. The estimated delivery is December 2025, with a contingency that delivery could shift slightly into January 2026. If timelines shift, the team commits to immediate notifications and monthly progress updates during development.

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds
Most funds are allocated to app development, with additional support for launch preparation and marketing. The team notes a buffer for unexpected costs to keep development the top priority.

## Risks & Challenges
The team cites typical software development risks such as potential delays or technical issues, mitigated by a scoped plan and monthly updates. Because rewards are mostly digital (codes or access), fulfillment risk is described as low, though minor delays in distributing access could occur. A health and wellness disclaimer clarifies that the project is not a substitute for medical treatment or diagnosis.

## Team & Partnerships
The effort is led by a sprint coach ("the founders"). The team plans to collaborate with athletes, coaches, and influencers to expand reach.

## What's Included
Backers receive primarily digital rewards, such as access codes.

## Technical Details
The campaign labels the technology as patent pending and repeatedly emphasizes AI-based video analysis for sprint mechanics. No device, OS, or hardware specs are provided.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans
The team promises ongoing updates during development and indicates that improvements will be delivered through the app over time.

## One-Sentence Summary

A mobile app that uses AI-powered video analysis to deliver sprint coaching feedback anytime, helping athletes improve form while enabling coaches and parents to track progress.

## Problem
The creators describe a consistent gap in sprint training: athletes often practice without timely feedback, while coaches lack bandwidth to analyze every block start or sprint repetition---especially when juggling other jobs or when athletes are traveling or on school breaks. This leaves athletes without guidance to progress safely and effectively when direct coaching isn't available.

## Solution / Product Overview
The product is presented as "a sprint coach in your pocket." It analyzes user-submitted sprint videos with AI to provide actionable feedback at any time. The aim is to let athletes see what's happening in their sprints, help coaches extend their impact without slowing practice, and assure parents that training is progressing safely.

## Key Features & Capabilities
- AI-powered video analysis of sprints.
- Feedback on block starts.
- Analysis of shin and torso angles.
- Insights into max-velocity mechanics.
- Positioning as a tool to complement---not replace---human coaching.
- A proposed tiered subscription model (e.g., free basic analysis, premium for detailed feedback) to be tested with a small group of early backers to validate pricing and features.

## Target Users & Use Cases
The campaign calls out athletes who train alone or while traveling, coaches seeking scalable analysis during practice, and parents looking for confidence in safe, continuous improvement.

## Development Status
The team states it has a working demo. Funds are intended to "complete and polish" the app into a user-ready tool, with a launch planned for the first wave of athletes, coaches, and parents.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan
Planned milestones include: finalizing the app, building specified analysis features (block starts, angle analysis, max-velocity mechanics), conducting a planned, limited pilot test with a specific, named high school or club track team to validate the app in a real-world coaching environment before full launch, proposing a test of a tiered subscription model with a small group of early backers to validate pricing and features, partnering with athletes/coaches/influencers to spread the word, and launching to an initial user group. The estimated delivery is December 2025, with a contingency that delivery could shift slightly into January 2026. If timelines shift, the team commits to immediate notifications and monthly progress updates during development.

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds
Most funds are allocated to app development, with additional support for launch preparation and marketing. The team notes a buffer for unexpected costs to keep development the top priority.

## Risks & Challenges
The team cites typical software development risks such as potential delays or technical issues, mitigated by a scoped plan and monthly updates. Because rewards are mostly digital (codes or access), fulfillment risk is described as low, though minor delays in distributing access could occur. A health and wellness disclaimer clarifies that the project is not a substitute for medical treatment or diagnosis.

## Team & Partnerships
The effort is led by a sprint coach ("the founders"). The team plans to collaborate with athletes, coaches, and influencers to expand reach.

## What's Included
Backers receive primarily digital rewards, such as access codes.

## Technical Details
The campaign labels the technology as patent pending and repeatedly emphasizes AI-based video analysis for sprint mechanics. No device, OS, or hardware specs are provided.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans
The team promises ongoing updates during development and indicates that improvements will be delivered through the app over time.

## One-Sentence Summary

A mobile app that uses AI-powered video analysis to deliver sprint coaching feedback anytime, helping athletes improve form while enabling coaches and parents to track progress.

## Problem
The creators describe a consistent gap in sprint training: athletes often practice without timely feedback, while coaches lack bandwidth to analyze every block start or sprint repetition---especially when juggling other jobs or when athletes are traveling or on school breaks. This leaves athletes without guidance to progress safely and effectively when direct coaching isn't available.

## Solution / Product Overview
The product is presented as "a sprint coach in your pocket." It analyzes user-submitted sprint videos with AI to provide actionable feedback at any time. The aim is to let athletes see what's happening in their sprints, help coaches extend their impact without slowing practice, and assure parents that training is progressing safely.

## Key Features & Capabilities
- AI-powered video analysis of sprints.
- Feedback on block starts.
- Analysis of shin and torso angles.
- Insights into max-velocity mechanics.
- Positioning as a tool to complement---not replace---human coaching.
- A proposed tiered subscription model (e.g., free basic analysis, premium for detailed feedback) to be tested with a small group of early backers to validate pricing and features.
- To illustrate the value concretely, the app is planned to provide specific, actionable feedback. For example, after analyzing a video, the AI might identify a sub-optimal shin angle at touchdown and suggest a specific drill, such as wicket runs, to help the athlete improve that aspect of their form.

## Target Users & Use Cases
The campaign calls out athletes who train alone or while traveling, coaches seeking scalable analysis during practice, and parents looking for confidence in safe, continuous improvement.

## Development Status
The team states it has a working demo. Funds are intended to "complete and polish" the app into a user-ready tool, with a launch planned for the first wave of athletes, coaches, and parents.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan
Planned milestones include: finalizing the app, building specified analysis features (block starts, angle analysis, max-velocity mechanics), conducting a planned, limited pilot test with a specific, named high school or club track team to validate the app in a real-world coaching environment before full launch, proposing a test of a tiered subscription model with a small group of early backers to validate pricing and features, partnering with athletes/coaches/influencers to spread the word, and launching to an initial user group. The estimated delivery is December 2025, with a contingency that delivery could shift slightly into January 2026. If timelines shift, the team commits to immediate notifications and monthly progress updates during development.

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds
Most funds are allocated to app development, with additional support for launch preparation and marketing. The team notes a buffer for unexpected costs to keep development the top priority.

## Risks & Challenges
The team cites typical software development risks such as potential delays or technical issues, mitigated by a scoped plan and monthly updates. Because rewards are mostly digital (codes or access), fulfillment risk is described as low, though minor delays in distributing access could occur. A health and wellness disclaimer clarifies that the project is not a substitute for medical treatment or diagnosis.

The effort is led by a sprint coach ("the founders"). The team plans to collaborate with athletes, coaches, and influencers to expand reach.

## What's Included
Backers receive primarily digital rewards, such as access codes.

## Technical Details
The campaign labels the technology as patent pending and repeatedly emphasizes AI-based video analysis for sprint mechanics. No device, OS, or hardware specs are provided.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans
The team promises ongoing updates during development and indicates that improvements will be delivered through the app over time.

The creators describe a consistent gap in sprint training: athletes often practice without timely feedback, while coaches lack bandwidth to analyze every block start or sprint repetition---especially when juggling other jobs or when athletes are traveling or on school breaks. This leaves athletes without guidance to progress safely and effectively when direct coaching isn't available.

## Solution / Product Overview
The product is presented as "a sprint coach in your pocket." It analyzes user-submitted sprint videos with AI to provide actionable feedback at any time. The aim is to let athletes see what's happening in their sprints, help coaches extend their impact without slowing practice, and assure parents that training is progressing safely.

## Key Features & Capabilities
- AI-powered video analysis of sprints.
- Feedback on block starts.
- Analysis of shin and torso angles.
- Insights into max-velocity mechanics.
- Positioning as a tool to complement---not replace---human coaching.
- A proposed tiered subscription model (e.g., free basic analysis, premium for detailed feedback) to be tested with a small group of early backers to validate pricing and features.
- To illustrate the value concretely, the app is planned to provide specific, actionable feedback. For example, after analyzing a video, the AI might identify a sub-optimal shin angle at touchdown and suggest a specific drill, such as wicket runs, to help the athlete improve that aspect of their form.

## Target Users & Use Cases
The campaign calls out athletes who train alone or while traveling, coaches seeking scalable analysis during practice, and parents looking for confidence in safe, continuous improvement.

## Development Status
The team states it has a working demo. Funds are intended to "complete and polish" the app into a user-ready tool, with a launch planned for the first wave of athletes, coaches, and parents.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan
Planned milestones include: finalizing the app, building specified analysis features (block starts, angle analysis, max-velocity mechanics), conducting a planned, limited pilot test with a specific, named high school or club track team to validate the app in a real-world coaching environment before full launch, proposing a test of a tiered subscription model with a small group of early backers to validate pricing and features, and a planned, specific test for analyzing a less common sprint event (e.g., the 400m hurdles start) to demonstrate roadmap breadth beyond basic sprints. Additional planned steps include partnering with athletes/coaches/influencers to spread the word, and launching to an initial user group. The estimated delivery is December 2025, with a contingency that delivery could shift slightly into January 2026. If timelines shift, the team commits to immediate notifications and monthly progress updates during development.

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds
Most funds are allocated to app development, with additional support for launch preparation and marketing. The team notes a buffer for unexpected costs to keep development the top priority.

Because rewards are mostly digital (codes or access), fulfillment risk is described as low, though minor delays in distributing access could occur. A health and wellness disclaimer clarifies that the project is not a substitute for medical treatment or diagnosis.

Backers receive primarily digital rewards, such as access codes.

The campaign labels the technology as patent pending and repeatedly emphasizes AI-based video analysis for sprint mechanics. No device, OS, or hardware specs are provided.

The team promises ongoing updates during development and indicates that improvements will be delivered through the app over time.

## One-Sentence Summary

A mobile app that uses AI-powered video analysis to deliver sprint coaching feedback anytime, helping athletes improve form while enabling coaches and parents to track progress.

## Problem
The creators describe a consistent gap in sprint training: athletes often practice without timely feedback, while coaches lack bandwidth to analyze every block start or sprint repetition---especially when juggling other jobs or when athletes are traveling or on school breaks. This leaves athletes without guidance to progress safely and effectively when direct coaching isn't available.

## Solution / Product Overview
The product is presented as "a sprint coach in your pocket." It analyzes user-submitted sprint videos with AI to provide actionable feedback at any time. The aim is to let athletes see what's happening in their sprints, help coaches extend their impact without slowing practice, and assure parents that training is progressing safely.

## Key Features & Capabilities
- AI-powered video analysis of sprints.
- Feedback on block starts.
- Analysis of shin and torso angles.
- Insights into max-velocity mechanics.
- Positioning as a tool to complement---not replace---human coaching.
- A proposed tiered subscription model (e.g., free basic analysis, premium for detailed feedback) to be tested with a small group of early backers to validate pricing and features.
- To illustrate the value concretely, the app is planned to provide specific, actionable feedback. For example, after analyzing a video, the AI might identify a sub-optimal shin angle at touchdown and suggest a specific drill, such as wicket runs, to help the athlete improve that aspect of their form.
- As a planned future initiative, we propose collaborating with a specific, named physical therapy or sports medicine professional to develop educational content on injury prevention, further enhancing the app's value for safe training.

## Target Users & Use Cases
The campaign calls out athletes who train alone or while traveling, coaches seeking scalable analysis during practice, and parents looking for confidence in safe, continuous improvement.

## Development Status
The team states it has a working demo. Funds are intended to "complete and polish" the app into a user-ready tool, with a launch planned for the first wave of athletes, coaches, and parents.

Planned milestones include: finalizing the app, building specified analysis features (block starts, angle analysis, max-velocity mechanics), conducting a planned, limited pilot test with a specific, named high school or club track team to validate the app in a real-world coaching environment before full launch, proposing a test of a tiered subscription model with a small group of early backers to validate pricing and features, proposing a planned collaboration with a specific, named physical therapy or sports medicine professional to develop content on injury prevention, partnering with athletes/coaches/influencers to spread the word, and launching to an initial user group. The estimated delivery is December 2025, with a contingency that delivery could shift slightly into January 2026. If timelines shift, the team commits to immediate notifications and monthly progress updates during development.

Most funds are allocated to app development, with additional support for launch preparation and marketing. The team notes a buffer for unexpected costs to keep development the top priority.

The team cites typical software development risks such as potential delays or technical issues, mitigated by a scoped plan and monthly updates. The effort is led by a sprint coach ("the founders"). The team plans to collaborate with athletes, coaches, and influencers to expand reach.

Backers receive primarily digital rewards, such as access codes.

## Technical Details
The campaign labels the technology as patent pending and repeatedly emphasizes AI-based video analysis for sprint mechanics. No device, OS, or hardware specs are provided.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans
The team promises ongoing updates during development and indicates that improvements will be delivered through the app over time.

## One-Sentence Summary

A mobile app that uses AI-powered video analysis to deliver sprint coaching feedback anytime, helping athletes improve form while enabling coaches and parents to track progress.

## Problem

The creators describe a consistent gap in sprint training: athletes often practice without timely feedback, while coaches lack bandwidth to analyze every block start or sprint repetition---especially when juggling other jobs or when athletes are traveling or on school breaks. This leaves athletes without guidance to progress safely and effectively when direct coaching isn't available.

## Solution / Product Overview

The product is presented as "a sprint coach in your pocket." It analyzes user-submitted sprint videos with AI to provide actionable feedback at any time. The aim is to let athletes see what's happening in their sprints, help coaches extend their impact without slowing practice, and assure parents that training is progressing safely.

## Key Features & Capabilities

- AI-powered video analysis of sprints.
- Feedback on block starts.
- Analysis of shin and torso angles.
- Insights into max-velocity mechanics.
- Positioning as a tool to complement---not replace---human coaching.

## One-Sentence Summary
A mobile app that uses AI-powered video analysis to deliver sprint coaching feedback anytime, helping athletes improve form while enabling coaches and parents to track progress.

## Problem
The creators describe a consistent gap in sprint training: athletes often practice without timely feedback, while coaches lack bandwidth to analyze every block start or sprint repetition---especially when juggling other jobs or when athletes are traveling or on school breaks. This leaves athletes without guidance to progress safely and effectively when direct coaching isn't available.

## Solution / Product Overview
The product is presented as "a sprint coach in your pocket." It analyzes user-submitted sprint videos with AI to provide actionable feedback at any time. The aim is to let athletes see what's happening in their sprints, help coaches extend their impact without slowing practice, and assure parents that training is progressing safely.

## Key Features & Capabilities
- AI-powered video analysis of sprints.
- Feedback on block starts.
- Analysis of shin and torso angles.
- Insights into max-velocity mechanics.
- Positioning as a tool to complement---not replace---human coaching.
- A proposed tiered subscription model (e.g., free basic analysis, premium for detailed feedback) to be tested with a small group of early backers to validate pricing and features.
- To illustrate the value concretely, the app is planned to provide specific, actionable feedback. For example, after analyzing a video, the AI might identify a sub-optimal shin angle at touchdown and suggest a specific drill, such as wicket runs, to help the athlete improve that aspect of their form.
- As a planned future initiative, we propose collaborating with a specific, named physical therapy or sports medicine professional to develop educational content on injury prevention, further enhancing the app's value for safe training.
- To clarify the development status, we propose creating a planned, short public demonstration video. This video would show the AI analyzing a single, anonymized sprint clip for one metric, such as shin angle.

## Target Users & Use Cases
The campaign calls out athletes who train alone or while traveling, coaches seeking scalable analysis during practice, and parents looking for confidence in safe, continuous improvement.

## Development Status
The team states it has a working demo. Funds are intended to "complete and polish" the app into a user-ready tool, with a launch planned for the first wave of athletes, coaches, and parents.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan
Planned milestones include: finalizing the app, building specified analysis features (block starts, angle analysis, max-velocity mechanics), creating a planned public demonstration video of the AI analyzing an anonymized sprint clip, conducting a planned, limited pilot test with a specific, named high school or club track team to validate the app in a real-world coaching environment before full launch, proposing a test of a tiered subscription model with a small group of early backers to validate pricing and features, proposing a planned collaboration with a specific, named physical therapy or sports medicine professional to develop content on injury prevention, partnering with athletes/coaches/influencers to spread the word, and launching to an initial user group. The estimated delivery is December 2025, with a contingency that delivery could shift slightly into January 2026. If timelines shift, the team commits to immediate notifications and monthly progress updates during development.

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds
Most funds are allocated to app development, with additional support for launch preparation and marketing. The team notes a buffer for unexpected costs to keep development the top priority.

## Risks & Challenges
The team cites typical software development risks such as potential delays or technical issues, mitigated by a scoped plan and monthly updates. Because rewards are mostly digital (codes or access), fulfillment risk is described as low, though minor delays in distributing access could occur. A health and wellness disclaimer clarifies that the project is not a substitute for medical treatment or diagnosis.

## Team & Partnerships
The effort is led by a sprint coach ("the founders"). The team plans to collaborate with athletes, coaches, and influencers to expand reach.

## What's Included
Backers receive primarily digital rewards, such as access codes.

## Technical Details
The campaign labels the technology as patent pending and repeatedly emphasizes AI-based video analysis for sprint mechanics. No device, OS, or hardware specs are provided. To increase transparency and trust in the technology, we propose publishing the methodology for a single AI analysis metric, such as shin angle, in a detailed blog post.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans
The team promises ongoing updates during development and indicates that improvements will be delivered through the app over time.

## One-Sentence Summary
A mobile app that uses AI-powered video analysis to deliver sprint coaching feedback anytime, helping athletes improve form while enabling coaches and parents to track progress.

## Problem
The creators describe a consistent gap in sprint training: athletes often practice without timely feedback, while coaches lack bandwidth to analyze every block start or sprint repetition---especially when juggling other jobs or when athletes are traveling or on school breaks. This leaves athletes without guidance to progress safely and effectively when direct coaching isn't available.

## Solution / Product Overview
The product is presented as "a sprint coach in your pocket." It analyzes user-submitted sprint videos with AI to provide actionable feedback at any time. The aim is to let athletes see what's happening in their sprints, help coaches extend their impact without slowing practice, and assure parents that training is progressing safely.

## Key Features & Capabilities
- AI-powered video analysis of sprints.
- Feedback on block starts.
- Analysis of shin and torso angles.
- Insights into max-velocity mechanics.
- Positioning as a tool to complement---not replace---human coaching.
- A proposed tiered subscription model (e.g., free basic analysis, premium for detailed feedback) to be tested with a small group of early backers to validate pricing and features.
- To illustrate the value concretely, the app is planned to provide specific, actionable feedback. For example, after analyzing a video, the AI might identify a sub-optimal shin angle at touchdown and suggest a specific drill, such as wicket runs, to help the athlete improve that aspect of their form.
- As a planned future initiative, we propose collaborating with a specific, named physical therapy or sports medicine professional to develop educational content on injury prevention, further enhancing the app's value for safe training.
- To clarify the development status, we propose creating a planned, short public demonstration video. This video would show the AI analyzing a single, anonymized sprint clip for one metric, such as shin angle.
- To demonstrate technical credibility, we propose publishing a detailed blog post outlining the methodology for a single AI analysis metric, such as shin angle. The planned outline for this post includes: an introduction explaining the importance of shin angle in sprinting; a high-level overview of the video processing pipeline; a detailed explanation of the computer vision model used for pose estimation; the specific algorithm for calculating the shin angle from keypoints; a discussion of validation methods and accuracy considerations; and a sample diagram illustrating the data flow from video upload to angle measurement.

## Target Users & Use Cases
The campaign calls out athletes who train alone or while traveling, coaches seeking scalable analysis during practice, and parents looking for confidence in safe, continuous improvement.

## Development Status
The team states it has a working demo. Funds are intended to "complete and polish" the app into a user-ready tool, with a launch planned for the first wave of athletes, coaches, and parents.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan
Planned milestones include: finalizing the app, building specified analysis features (block starts, angle analysis, max-velocity mechanics), creating a planned public demonstration video of the AI analyzing an anonymized sprint clip, conducting a planned, limited pilot test with a specific, named high school or club track team to validate the app in a real-world coaching environment before full launch, proposing a test of a tiered subscription model with a small group of early backers to validate pricing and features, proposing a planned collaboration with a specific, named physical therapy or sports medicine professional to develop content on injury prevention, publishing the proposed blog post on shin angle methodology, partnering with athletes/coaches/influencers to spread the word, and launching to an initial user group. The estimated delivery is December 2025, with a contingency that delivery could shift slightly into January 2026. If timelines shift, the team commits to immediate notifications and monthly progress updates during development.

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds
Most funds are allocated to app development, with additional support for launch preparation and marketing. The team notes a buffer for unexpected costs to keep development the top priority.

## Risks & Challenges
The team cites typical software development risks such as potential delays or technical issues, mitigated by a scoped plan and monthly updates. Because rewards are mostly digital (codes or access), fulfillment risk is described as low, though minor delays in distributing access could occur. A health and wellness disclaimer clarifies that the project is not a substitute for medical treatment or diagnosis.

## Team & Partnerships
The effort is led by a sprint coach ("the founders"). The team plans to collaborate with athletes, coaches, and influencers to expand reach.

## What's Included
Backers receive primarily digital rewards, such as access codes.

## Technical Details
The campaign labels the technology as patent pending and repeatedly emphasizes AI-based video analysis for sprint mechanics. No device, OS, or hardware specs are provided. To increase transparency and trust in the technology, we propose publishing the methodology for a single AI analysis metric, such as shin angle, in a detailed blog post, as outlined in the Key Features.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans
The team promises ongoing updates during development and indicates that improvements will be delivered through the app over time.

The creators describe a consistent gap in sprint training: athletes often practice without timely feedback, while coaches lack bandwidth to analyze every block start or sprint repetition---especially when juggling other jobs or when athletes are traveling or on school breaks. This leaves athletes without guidance to progress safely and effectively when direct coaching isn't available.

## Solution / Product Overview
The product is presented as "a sprint coach in your pocket." It analyzes user-submitted sprint videos with AI to provide actionable feedback at any time. The aim is to let athletes see what's happening in their sprints, help coaches extend their impact without slowing practice, and assure parents that training is progressing safely.

## Key Features & Capabilities
- AI-powered video analysis of sprints.
- Feedback on block starts.
- Analysis of shin and torso angles.
- Insights into max-velocity mechanics.
- Positioning as a tool to complement---not replace---human coaching.
- A proposed tiered subscription model (e.g., free basic analysis, premium for detailed feedback) to be tested with a small group of early backers to validate pricing and features.
- To illustrate the value concretely, the app is planned to provide specific, actionable feedback. For example, after analyzing a video, the AI might identify a sub-optimal shin angle at touchdown and suggest a specific drill, such as wicket runs, to help the athlete improve that aspect of their form.
- As a planned future initiative, we propose collaborating with a specific, named physical therapy or sports medicine professional to develop educational content on injury prevention, further enhancing the app's value for safe training.
- To clarify the development status, we propose creating a planned, short public demonstration video. This video would show the AI analyzing a single, anonymized sprint clip for one metric, such as shin angle.

The planned outline for this post includes: an introduction explaining the importance of shin angle in sprinting; a high-level overview of the video processing pipeline; a detailed explanation of the computer vision model used for pose estimation; the specific algorithm for calculating the shin angle from keypoints; a discussion of validation methods and accuracy considerations; and a sample diagram illustrating the data flow from video upload to angle measurement.
- As a planned, limited-time offer for early backers, we propose allowing them to vote on which one additional analysis metric (e.g., arm carriage, ground contact time) should be prioritized for development after the core features are complete.

The campaign calls out athletes who train alone or while traveling, coaches seeking scalable analysis during practice, and parents looking for confidence in safe, continuous improvement.

## Development Status

## One-Sentence Summary
A mobile app that uses AI-powered video analysis to deliver sprint coaching feedback anytime, helping athletes improve form while enabling coaches and parents to track progress.

## Problem
The creators describe a consistent gap in sprint training: athletes often practice without timely feedback, while coaches lack bandwidth to analyze every block start or sprint repetition---especially when juggling other jobs or when athletes are traveling or on school breaks. This leaves athletes without guidance to progress safely and effectively when direct coaching isn't available.

## Solution / Product Overview
The product is presented as "a sprint coach in your pocket." It analyzes user-submitted sprint videos with AI to provide actionable feedback at any time. The aim is to let athletes see what's happening in their sprints, help coaches extend their impact without slowing practice, and assure parents that training is progressing safely.

## Key Features & Capabilities
- AI-powered video analysis of sprints.
- Feedback on block starts.
- Analysis of shin and torso angles.
- Insights into max-velocity mechanics.
- Positioning as a tool to complement---not replace---human coaching.
- A proposed tiered subscription model (e.g., free basic analysis, premium for detailed feedback) to be tested with a small group of early backers to validate pricing and features.
- To illustrate the value concretely, the app is planned to provide specific, actionable feedback. For example, after analyzing a video, the AI might identify a sub-optimal shin angle at touchdown and suggest a specific drill, such as wicket runs, to help the athlete improve that aspect of their form.
- As a planned future initiative, we propose collaborating with a specific, named physical therapy or sports medicine professional to develop educational content on injury prevention, further enhancing the app's value for safe training.
- To validate the safety and appropriateness of the suggested corrective drills before the planned pilot test, we propose a small, targeted test of the app's feedback with a specific, named local physical therapist.
- To clarify the development status, we propose creating a planned, short public demonstration video. This video would show the AI analyzing a single, anonymized sprint clip for one metric, such as shin angle.
- To demonstrate technical credibility, we propose publishing a detailed blog post outlining the methodology for a single AI analysis metric, such as shin angle. The planned outline for this post includes: an introduction explaining the importance of shin angle in sprinting; a high-level overview of the video processing pipeline; a detailed explanation of the computer vision model used for pose estimation; the specific algorithm for calculating the shin angle from keypoints; a discussion of validation methods and accuracy considerations; and a sample diagram illustrating the data flow from video upload to angle measurement.

## Target Users & Use Cases
The campaign calls out athletes who train alone or while traveling, coaches seeking scalable analysis during practice, and parents looking for confidence in safe, continuous improvement.

## Development Status
The team states it has a working demo. Funds are intended to "complete and polish" the app into a user-ready tool, with a launch planned for the first wave of athletes, coaches, and parents.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan
Planned milestones include: finalizing the app, building specified analysis features (block starts, angle analysis, max-velocity mechanics), creating a planned public demonstration video of the AI analyzing an anonymized sprint clip, conducting a planned, limited pilot test with a specific, named high school or club track team to validate the app in a real-world coaching environment before full launch, proposing a test of a tiered subscription model with a small group of early backers to validate pricing and features, proposing a planned collaboration with a specific, named physical therapy or sports medicine professional to develop content on injury prevention, publishing the proposed blog post on shin angle methodology, partnering with athletes/coaches/influencers to spread the word, and launching to an initial user group. As part of the preparation for the pilot, we propose the small, targeted test of the app's feedback with a specific, named local physical therapist. The estimated delivery is December 2025, with a contingency that delivery could shift slightly into January 2026. If timelines shift, the team commits to immediate notifications and monthly progress updates during development.

## Why Crowdfunding / Use of Funds
Most funds are allocated to app development, with additional support for launch preparation and marketing. The team notes a buffer for unexpected costs to keep development the top priority.

## Risks & Challenges
The team cites typical software development risks such as potential delays or technical issues, mitigated by a scoped plan and monthly updates. Because rewards are mostly digital (codes or access), fulfillment risk is described as low, though minor delays in distributing access could occur. A health and wellness disclaimer clarifies that the project is not a substitute for medical treatment or diagnosis.

## Team & Partnerships
The effort is led by a sprint coach ("the founders"). The team plans to collaborate with athletes, coaches, and influencers to expand reach.

## What's Included
Backers receive primarily digital rewards, such as access codes.

## Technical Details
The campaign labels the technology as patent pending and repeatedly emphasizes AI-based video analysis for sprint mechanics. No device, OS, or hardware specs are provided. To increase transparency and trust in the technology, we propose publishing the methodology for a single AI analysis metric, such as shin angle, in a detailed blog post, as outlined in the Key Features.

## Support & Post-Launch Plans
The team promises ongoing updates during development and indicates that improvements will be delivered through the app over time.

The creators describe a consistent gap in sprint training: athletes often practice without timely feedback, while coaches lack bandwidth to analyze every block start or sprint repetition---especially when juggling other jobs or when athletes are traveling or on school breaks. ## Solution / Product Overview
The product is presented as "a sprint coach in your pocket." It analyzes user-submitted sprint videos with AI to provide actionable feedback at any time. The aim is to let athletes see what's happening in their sprints, help coaches extend their impact without slowing practice, and assure parents that training is progressing safely.

## Key Features & Capabilities
- AI-powered video analysis of sprints.
- Feedback on block starts.
- Analysis of shin and torso angles.
- Insights into max-velocity mechanics.
- Positioning as a tool to complement---not replace---human coaching.
- A proposed tiered subscription model (e.g., free basic analysis, premium for detailed feedback) to be tested with a small group of early backers to validate pricing and features.
- To illustrate the value concretely, the app is planned to provide specific, actionable feedback. For example, after analyzing a video, the AI might identify a sub-optimal shin angle at touchdown and suggest a specific drill, such as wicket runs, to help the athlete improve that aspect of their form.
- As a planned future initiative, we propose collaborating with a specific, named physical therapy or sports medicine professional to develop educational content on injury prevention, further enhancing the app's value for safe training.
- To validate the safety and appropriateness of the suggested corrective drills before the planned pilot test, we propose a small, targeted test of the app's feedback with a specific, named local physical therapist.
- To clarify the development status, we propose creating a planned, short public demonstration video. This video would show the AI analyzing a single, anonymized sprint clip for one metric, such as shin angle.
- To demonstrate technical credibility, we propose publishing a detailed blog post outlining the methodology for a single AI analysis metric, such as shin angle. - To address common user concerns, we propose creating a planned, public FAQ document addressing data privacy, video storage, and how user data is used for AI training, to be published alongside the demonstration video.

The campaign calls out athletes who train alone or while traveling, coaches seeking scalable analysis during practice, and parents looking for confidence in safe, continuous improvement.

The team states it has a working demo. Funds are intended to "complete and polish" the app into a user-ready tool, with a launch planned for the first wave of athletes, coaches, and parents.

As part of the preparation for the pilot, we propose the small, targeted test of the app's feedback with a specific, named local physical therapist. Most funds are allocated to app development, with additional support for launch preparation and marketing. The team notes a buffer for unexpected costs to keep development the top priority.

The team cites typical software development risks such as potential delays or technical issues, mitigated by a scoped plan and monthly updates. The effort is led by a sprint coach ("the founders"). The team plans to collaborate with athletes, coaches, and influencers to expand reach.

Backers receive primarily digital rewards, such as access codes.

The team promises ongoing updates during development and indicates that improvements will be delivered through the app over time.

- To further explore validation of the AI's accuracy, we propose a planned, specific outreach to a named, local university's sports science department to explore a potential future collaboration for validating the AI's accuracy against motion capture data.

## Target Users & Use Cases
The campaign calls out athletes who train alone or while traveling, coaches seeking scalable analysis during practice, and parents looking for confidence in safe, continuous improvement.

## Development Status
The team states it has a working demo. Funds are intended to "complete and polish" the app into a user-ready tool, with a launch planned for the first wave of athletes, coaches, and parents.

Planned milestones include: finalizing the app, building specified analysis features (block starts, angle analysis, max-velocity mechanics), creating a planned public demonstration video of the AI analyzing an anonymized sprint clip, publishing the proposed public FAQ document on data privacy and usage, conducting a planned, limited pilot test with a specific, named high school or club track team to validate the app in a real-world coaching environment before full launch, proposing a test of a tiered subscription model with a small group of early backers to validate pricing and features, proposing a planned collaboration with a specific, named physical therapy or sports medicine professional to develop content on injury prevention, publishing the proposed blog post on shin angle methodology, proposing a planned, specific outreach to a named, local university's sports science department to explore a potential future collaboration for validating the AI's accuracy against motion capture data, partnering with athletes/coaches/influencers to spread the word, and launching to an initial user group. Most funds are allocated to app development, with additional support for launch preparation and marketing. The team notes a buffer for unexpected costs to keep development the top priority.

The team cites typical software development risks such as potential delays or technical issues, mitigated by a scoped plan and monthly updates. The effort is led by a sprint coach ("the founders"). The team plans to collaborate with athletes, coaches, and influencers to expand reach.

Backers receive primarily digital rewards, such as access codes.

## One-Sentence Summary
A mobile app that uses AI-powered video analysis to deliver sprint coaching feedback anytime, helping athletes improve form while enabling coaches and parents to track progress.

## Problem
The creators describe a consistent gap in sprint training: athletes often practice without timely feedback, while coaches lack bandwidth to analyze every block start or sprint repetition---especially when juggling other jobs or when athletes are traveling or on school breaks. This leaves athletes without guidance to progress safely and effectively when direct coaching isn't available.

## Solution / Product Overview
The product is presented as "a sprint coach in your pocket." It analyzes user-submitted sprint videos with AI to provide actionable feedback at any time. The aim is to let athletes see what's happening in their sprints, help coaches extend their impact without slowing practice, and assure parents that training is progressing safely.

## Key Features & Capabilities
- AI-powered video analysis of sprints.
- Feedback on block starts.
- Analysis of shin and torso angles.
- Insights into max-velocity mechanics.
- Positioning as a tool to complement---not replace---human coaching.
- A proposed tiered subscription model (e.g., free basic analysis, premium for detailed feedback) to be tested with a small group of early backers to validate pricing and features.
- To illustrate the value concretely, the app is planned to provide specific, actionable feedback. For example, after analyzing a video, the AI might identify a sub-optimal shin angle at touchdown and suggest a specific drill, such as wicket runs, to help the athlete improve that aspect of their form.
- As a planned future initiative, we propose collaborating with a specific, named physical therapy or sports medicine professional to develop educational content on injury prevention, further enhancing the app's value for safe training.
- To validate the safety and appropriateness of the suggested corrective drills before the planned pilot test, we propose a small, targeted test of the app's feedback with a specific, named local physical therapist.
- To clarify the development status, we propose creating a planned, short public demonstration video. This video would show the AI analyzing a single, anonymized sprint clip for one metric, such as shin angle.
- To further illustrate how the app complements human coaching, we propose creating a planned, short comparison video showing the AI's analysis of the same sprint clip side-by-side with a coach's verbal feedback.
- To demonstrate technical credibility, we propose publishing a detailed blog post outlining the methodology for a single AI analysis metric, such as shin angle. The planned outline for this post includes: an introduction explaining the importance of shin angle in sprinting; a high-level overview of the video processing pipeline; a detailed explanation of the computer vision model used for pose estimation; the specific algorithm for calculating the shin angle from keypoints; a discussion of validation methods and accuracy considerations; and a sample diagram illustrating the data flow from video upload to angle measurement.
- To address common user concerns, we propose creating a planned, public FAQ document addressing data privacy, video storage, and how user data is used for AI training, to be published alongside the demonstration video.
- To further explore validation of the AI's accuracy, we propose a planned, specific outreach to a named, local university's sports science department to explore a potential future collaboration for validating the AI's accuracy against motion capture data.

## Target Users & Use Cases
The campaign calls out athletes who train alone or while traveling, coaches seeking scalable analysis during practice, and parents looking for confidence in safe, continuous improvement.

## Development Status
The team states it has a working demo. Funds are intended to "complete and polish" the app into a user-ready tool, with a launch planned for the first wave of athletes, coaches, and parents.

## Roadmap & Delivery Plan
Planned milestones include: finalizing the app, building specified analysis features (block starts, angle analysis, max-velocity mechanics), creating a planned public demonstration video of the AI analyzing an anonymized sprint clip, creating the proposed comparison video illustrating AI and coach feedback side-by-side, publishing the proposed public FAQ document on data privacy and usage, conducting a planned, limited pilot test with a specific, named high school or club track team to validate the app in a real-world coaching environment before full launch, proposing a test of a tiered subscription model with a small group of early backers to validate pricing and features, proposing a planned collaboration with a specific, named physical therapy or sports medicine professional to develop content on injury prevention, publishing the proposed blog post on shin angle methodology, proposing a planned, specific outreach to a named, local university's sports science department to explore a potential future collaboration for validating the AI's accuracy against motion capture data, partnering with athletes/coaches/influencers to spread the word, and launching to an initial user group. As part of the preparation for the pilot, we propose the small, targeted test of the app's feedback with a specific, named local physical therapist. The estimated delivery is December 2025, with a contingency that delivery could shift slightly into January 2026. If timelines shift, the team commits to immediate notifications and monthly progress updates during development.

Most funds are allocated to app development, with additional support for launch preparation and marketing. The team notes a buffer for unexpected costs to keep development the top priority.

Because rewards are mostly digital (codes or access), fulfillment risk is described as low, though minor delays in distributing access could occur. A health and wellness disclaimer clarifies that the project is not a substitute for medical treatment or diagnosis.
